findings.failure_path: From a marked checkout, run a Python heredoc containing only print("open('hooks/gate.py', 'w')"). This merely prints an example, but _code_targets matches the call inside the string and returns the shared path. With the owner unloaded, the hook denies this read-only command and spends the attempt intended for a later edit. Calling this an accepted precision gap in the candidate does not satisfy the frozen acceptance.
findings.smallest_fix: Match executable call nodes using Python's stdlib AST; conservatively exclude string contents for other supported interpreters. Add a printed-example control asserting zero attempts.

findings.failure_path: The valid command `(printf x)>hooks/gate.py` overwrites the shared file. shlex groups the adjacent punctuation as `)>`, which passes neither the separator test nor the redirection test. No target is returned, so the checkpoint is bypassed. `printf x;>hooks/gate.py` has the same failure with `;>`.
findings.smallest_fix: Separate punctuation runs into actual shell operators before segment dispatch, preserving compound operators such as >> and &&. Add adjacent group/redirection and separator/redirection regression cases.

findings.failure_path: `perl -pi -e's/a/b/' hooks/gate.py` performs an in-place edit, but scripted recognises only a standalone -e. _operands discards the attached script option, leaving only the filename; files[1:] then drops that filename. GNU sed with an attached -e expression has the same bypass.
findings.smallest_fix: Recognise attached script-option values before deciding whether the first operand is a script. Add positive cases for Perl -eSCRIPT and GNU sed -eSCRIPT.

findings.failure_path: With a tracked draft.py at the checkout root, `git mv draft.py hooks/` creates hooks/draft.py. The extractor returns only the root-level source and the destination directory; neither qualifies as a shared source-file target. This supported git mv form therefore receives no checkpoint.
findings.smallest_fix: For git mv directory destinations, derive each destination filename from its source basename while retaining source targets. Add a root-to-hooks move case.

findings.failure_path: `bash -n -c 'echo x > hooks/gate.py'` checks syntax without executing the redirection. The nested-shell branch ignores -n and recursively collects the inner target, denying a read-only syntax check and consuming the shared attempt.
findings.smallest_fix: Respect noexec options before -c when extracting nested-shell targets, while retaining genuine outer-shell redirections. Add a syntax-check control asserting zero attempts.

findings.failure_path: On GNU env, `env -C /tmp touch hooks/gate.py` writes under /tmp when /tmp/hooks exists. The wrapper loop consumes -C and its value without changing the wrapped command's cwd, so it reports the checkout's hooks/gate.py instead. An off-surface write consequently spends the checkpoint.
findings.smallest_fix: Apply wrapper-specific directory options to wrapped-command operands, keeping outer redirections relative to the caller. Add an off-surface env -C control.

findings.failure_path: Evidence gap: the only large-input control exceeds 64 KiB and returns immediately. It does not establish the required 10-second containment for accepted inputs with many operands, deep paths, or expensive filesystem resolution. The parser performs realpath, directory checks, and shared-marker probes without a demonstrated runtime budget.
findings.smallest_fix: Supply candidate-bound timing and timeout-containment results for synthetic near-limit inputs through the guard. Add bounded-work bailouts if those cases exceed the available hook budget.

concern_results.conclusion: Static tracing finds recognised writes that bypass detection and read-only/off-surface commands that consume the attempt. The added tests omit these counterexamples. The 5a no-mechanism decision and measurement record are present.

Both tool paths share the atomic implementation-lane claim; existing engine deny/ask decisions return before parsing, and the loaded-owner skip precedes claiming. No command execution is introduced. Ordinary exception fallback is visible, but containment within the 10-second timeout lacks evidence.

challenge_focus: Try to break the shell-write checkpoint: find a common agent shell command that writes a markdown or source file under a ccl-skills checkout's skills/, hooks/ or scripts/ yet yields no target, or a read-only or off-surface command that yields a shared target and so spends the single per-context attempt. Also attack attempt sharing with the edit tools, precedence of an existing engine deny/ask, exceptions escaping handle(), cost on large or hostile input under the 10 s hook timeout, and any way the parser executes or expands command text. Context after candidate_bytes is the full current hook and guard for reference.
